reviewedRef: 20-device-feedback-round-1-polish-theme-simplification-identity (PR #24, slices 10-25) vs main -- DATA & BACKGROUND domain
summary: FAIL. Three blocking defects, all on the backup/import path and all in the data-loss class this repo has been bitten by before. (1) importDatabase deletes its rollback copy at backup_service.dart:201 before the imported file is ever opened at :236, and :236-239 sit outside the try -- any reopen failure leaves the user with no original database and no backup, and throws a raw exception the UI cannot classify. (2) PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL) returns a busy result row rather than throwing, so the catch at :172 never fires; the -wal is then deleted unconditionally at :194 while the rollback copy at :185 holds only the main file, so the documented swapFailed rollback silently restores a state missing every WAL-only commit -- reachable because the WorkManager auto-backup and notification background isolates each open their own connection to the same file. (3) Nothing on the import path reads PRAGMA user_version, so a newer-schema backup is accepted; the onUpgrade chain has only 'from < N' guards and no downgrade guard, so the file either kills the app past the point of no return or is silently stamped back to v4, arming a permanent 'duplicate column name' failure on the next real upgrade. Beyond those: three DST/Duration-arithmetic defects in stats_calculator (week boundaries drop or double-count completions; streak over-counts and median cadence under-reports across spring-forward) that repeat the exact mistake recurrence_calculator was fixed for; a voice change that updates the notification channel but never reschedules, so pending reminders keep the old voice's title/body/actions; and @TableIndex indexes that only ever exist on fresh installs, including never on an imported legacy backup. Migration upgrade paths themselves (v1/v2/v3 -> v4), the recurrence calculator's DST and month-clamping arithmetic, double-completion idempotence, DriftRemoteException unwrapping, and voice/intent parsing all probed clean. NOTE: this session had no shell, so 'flutter test' and probe tests could not be run; every finding is derived from source reading and explicit arithmetic. No workspace files were modified.

findings.claim: importDatabase deletes the pre-import rollback backup before the imported database has ever been opened, and the reopen/repair/reschedule steps sit outside the try -- any post-swap failure destroys the user's data with no rollback
findings.detail: Line 197 renames the staging file over the live database; 198 runs the test seam; 200-202 delete backupFile; 230-232 close the try/finally; 236 is the FIRST open of the imported file (repairInvalidCustomDaysRecurrence), followed by rescheduleAll() at 238 and sync() at 239 -- all three outside the try. isValidChoreBuddyDatabase (backup_validation.dart:22-36) only lists sqlite_master table names and reads no data page, so a file with an intact schema but truncated/corrupt chores b-tree pages passes. Such a file is producible by exportDatabase itself: backup_service.dart:97 is a bare dbFile.copy() with no post-copy validation, unlike writeAutoBackupSnapshot. Repro: pick such a file -> validation passes (:156) -> live db closed (:175) -> sidecars deleted (:194) -> rename (:197) -> backup deleted (:201) -> :236 throws SqliteException(11) 'database disk image is malformed' -> exception escapes importDatabase raw (not an ImportException, so no ImportFailureReason for the UI) with the original database overwritten and its only copy already deleted. Same class as the previously-caught disk-full import, relocated to the window after the try rather than inside it. Fix: move 236-239 inside the try and defer the backupFile.delete() until after a successful reopen-and-read; add a data-touching check (SELECT count(*) FROM chores or PRAGMA quick_check) to isValidChoreBuddyDatabase so corrupt files are rejected before the point of no return.

findings.claim: A failed WAL checkpoint is invisible (the PRAGMA returns busy rather than throwing) and the -wal is then deleted unconditionally, so the swapFailed rollback restores a database missing every WAL-only commit
findings.detail: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL) returns a result row (busy, log, checkpointed) with busy=1 under reader contention; it does not raise. customStatement therefore succeeds and the catch at :172 never fires -- the debugPrint at :173 is dead code for the common failure. Contention is real: autoBackupCallbackDispatcher (auto_backup_task.dart:38) and notificationBackgroundResponseHandler (background_completion.dart:126) each construct their own AppDatabase() against the same file from separate background isolates. Repro: WorkManager auto-backup holds a read lock while the user imports. (1) :171 returns busy=1; recent commits remain WAL-only. (2) :184 records preSwapLength and :185 copies ONLY chore_buddy.sqlite to .pre-import.bak -- a snapshot missing those commits. (3) :194 _deleteSidecarFiles deletes the -wal; those commits are now gone from disk. (4) :197 rename fails (ENOSPC / permissions / partial staging copy at :188). (5) _isRestorableBackup (:247-251) passes -- it compares the backup against the same WAL-less main file it was copied from, so the length check cannot detect the loss -- and the backup is copied back. (6) ImportException(swapFailed) is thrown, whose doc at :26-29 promises the pre-swap state was restored. It was not: everything WAL-only at step 1 is permanently lost and nothing reports it. Fix: read the checkpoint's result row and abort before :184 when busy != 0; and copy/restore -wal and -shm alongside the main file.

findings.claim: Import never checks PRAGMA user_version, and onUpgrade has no downgrade guard -- a newer-schema backup either kills the app past the point of no return or is silently stamped back to v4, arming a permanent 'duplicate column name' failure
findings.detail: isValidChoreBuddyDatabase checks only that sqlite_master lists chores/tags/completion_records/chore_tags; it never reads PRAGMA user_version, and nothing else on the import path does either. So a .db3 written by a future build with schemaVersion 5 is accepted and swapped in at backup_service.dart:197. app_database.dart:29-40 is a chain of one-way 'from < N' guards with no onDowngrade and no 'from > to' rejection. At the first open (backup_service.dart:236) exactly one of two things happens, both unrecoverable: (a) drift routes the mismatch into onUpgrade(m, 5, 4) -- its OpeningDetails.hadUpgrade is a versionBefore != versionNow comparison, not '<' -- all three guards evaluate false, the migration is a silent no-op, and drift stamps user_version = 4 onto a physically-v5 file; the import appears to succeed, and when the user later updates to the build that IS v5, onUpgrade(m, 4, 5) runs addColumn for a column that already exists -> SqliteException 'duplicate column name' on EVERY open, forever, recoverable only by clearing app data; or (b) drift throws on the downgrade, which lands at :236 -- after the swap and after the backup was deleted (see finding 1), so the original database is gone. I could not execute drift's open path to determine which branch fires (no shell in this session; pub cache not readable), but the finding is independent of that: nothing in this codebase rejects user_version > schemaVersion. The upgrade direction is correct and covered by database_migration_test.dart for v1->v4, v2->v4 and v3->v4; only the downgrade direction is unguarded and untested. Fix: read PRAGMA user_version on the existing read-only handle in isValidChoreBuddyDatabase and reject anything above AppDatabase().schemaVersion with integrityCheckFailed -- before the live file is touched -- plus an explicit 'if (from > to) throw' in onUpgrade.

findings.claim: Week boundaries are computed with Duration arithmetic across DST, so completions near a transition fall into no week (fall-back) or into two (spring-forward)
findings.detail: recurrence_calculator.dart:63-68 documents this exact hazard and uses calendar-component arithmetic to avoid it; stats_calculator.dart uses Duration at :11, :42, :71 and :191 and does not. Repro (America/New_York, DST ends Sun 2 Nov 2025 02:00 EDT -> 01:00 EST): now = Fri 31 Oct 2025 12:00 -> startOfWeek = Oct 27 00:00 EDT (correct). countCompletionsInWeek computes weekEnd = weekStart.add(Duration(days: 7)) at :42; Oct 27 00:00 EDT = Oct 27 04:00 UTC, +168h = Nov 3 04:00 UTC = Sun Nov 2 23:00 EST -- an hour early, because Nov 2 was a 25-hour day. A completion at Sun 2 Nov 23:30 EST satisfies !isBefore(weekStart) but fails isBefore(weekEnd), so it is excluded from its own week; the next week's startOfWeek is Nov 3 00:00 EST, which is after it, so it is excluded there too. The completion is counted in ZERO weeks and disappears from both the banner's weekly line and the Mission Log bars. Mirror case: across a spring-forward, weekStart + 168h lands an hour PAST the true next Monday 00:00, double-counting that hour into two weeks. Separately at :71, thisWeekStart(Nov 3 00:00 EST).subtract(Duration(days: 7)) = Oct 27 01:00 EDT, not Oct 27 00:00, so Monday-00:00-to-01:00 completions are silently missing from the last-week comparison weekDeltaKind depends on. weeklyCompletionCounts (:191) compounds this over a 12-week window. startOfWeek itself (:11) is safe only by the accident that a Monday-based week walked back from any day never crosses a Sunday transition -- an accident that does not hold where the transition is not on a Sunday (e.g. Iran) or falls at 00:00 local. stats_calculator_test.dart:26-39 tests only a non-transition week. Fix: reuse recurrence_calculator's calendar-component _addDays for every week-boundary computation.

findings.claim: computeStreak and medianCadenceDays use difference().inDays between local midnights, which truncates on a 23-hour day: streaks over-count and median cadence under-reports across a spring-forward
findings.detail: _dateOnly(a).difference(_dateOnly(b)).inDays measures elapsed hours / 24, not calendar days, so a span crossing a spring-forward is one hour short and truncates down. Repro (streak): US spring-forward Sun 8 Mar 2026 02:00; a daily chore has expectedPeriod = 1 and maxGap = 2 (:107). Completions Fri 6 Mar 09:00 and Mon 9 Mar 09:00 are 3 calendar days apart, which exceeds the 2-day grace and must break the streak. _dateOnly gives Mar 6 00:00 EST (Mar 6 05:00 UTC) and Mar 9 00:00 EDT (Mar 9 04:00 UTC); difference = 71h; .inDays = 2; gap <= maxGap, so the streak wrongly continues and the user is credited with an unearned daily streak. Repro (cadence, :131): a weekly chore with completions exactly 7 calendar days apart spanning the same transition yields 167h -> .inDays = 6, so medianCadenceDays returns 6.0 for a strictly weekly chore; feeding that to cadenceScheduleFor (:145-150) can report a chore genuinely drifting to 8-day intervals as onSchedule. Fix: round the hour delta ((a.difference(b).inHours / 24).round()) or normalise both dates through DateTime.utc(y, m, d) before subtracting so the local offset cancels.

findings.claim: Switching voice updates the notification channel but never reschedules, so every already-scheduled reminder still fires with the old voice's title, body and action labels
findings.detail: _onVoiceChanged calls scheduler.updateChannel(...) and widgetSyncService.sync(), and its comment at :110-115 claims recreating the channel is 'enough for both already-scheduled and future reminders to pick up the new copy'. That is true only of the channel's name/description as shown in Android system settings. scheduleChoreNotification bakes strings.notificationTitle(chore.name), strings.notificationBody, strings.notificationCompleteAction and strings.notificationSnoozeAction into the zonedSchedule call (notification_service.dart:34-42), and flutter_local_notifications persists those strings with the pending alarm; updateChannel (notification_scheduler.dart:141-164) only recreates the AndroidNotificationChannel and cannot rewrite a scheduled payload. Repro: Superhero voice active, a chore due tomorrow has a reminder scheduled with Superhero copy; user switches to Grandma; the channel is renamed and the widget re-synced; tomorrow the reminder fires in Superhero's voice with Superhero's Complete/Not Today button labels, and stays wrong until that chore happens to be mutated by some other flow. Fix: add 'await ref.read(notificationServiceProvider).rescheduleAll();' to _onVoiceChanged -- the method exists for exactly this -- and correct the comment.

findings.claim: @TableIndex indexes are created only by onCreate, so every upgraded install and every imported legacy backup runs permanently without them
findings.detail: idx_completion_records_chore_id (tables.dart:33) and idx_chore_tags_tag_id (tables.dart:51) materialise as Index entries in allSchemaEntities (app_database.g.dart:1413-1420), which means only Migrator.createAll() -- i.e. onCreate -- creates them. onUpgrade adds columns and nothing else; grep for createIndex / Index( across the repo hits only tables.dart and the generated file. Repro: any install upgrading from a build that predates the annotations runs the three addColumn steps, reaches user_version 4, reports a fully-migrated schema, and never gets either index. The import path makes this reachable on a brand-new install too: importing a v1/v2/v3 backup routes through onUpgrade and never onCreate, so the swapped-in database is stamped v4 with no indexes; watchHistoryForChore and the Mission Log's per-chore grouping then table-scan completion_records for the life of the install. database_migration_test.dart cannot catch it -- every fixture is built via createAll and only has columns dropped. Note the generated DDL is plain CREATE INDEX (not IF NOT EXISTS), so a naive m.createAll() in onUpgrade would fail on installs that already have them; the fix must be version-gated. Fix: bump schemaVersion to 5, add 'if (from < 5) { await m.create(idxCompletionRecordsChoreId); await m.create(idxChoreTagsTagId); }', and assert index presence in sqlite_master after an upgrade in the migration test.

findings.claim: Auto-backup writes and 'validates' snapshots that can silently omit recent commits, then rotates older good snapshots away
findings.detail: Same root cause as the import checkpoint finding, different blast radius. :64 issues PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL) and ignores its result row (it returns busy rather than raising). :70 copies only dbFile -- no -wal. :72 validates the copy with isValidChoreBuddyDatabase, which reads sqlite_master and nothing else, so a snapshot missing a week of completions validates as good. :81 then calls rotateAutoBackups, which deletes everything past the newest 5. Repro: the WorkManager job fires while the app is foregrounded with an open drift connection; the FULL checkpoint returns busy=1 and recent commits stay WAL-only; the copy captures only the main file; validation passes on table names; rotation deletes the oldest snapshot. Repeat across 5 consecutive days of contention and every retained snapshot is stale in the same way -- the recovery set is silently hollowed out while lastAutoBackupAt (auto_backup_task.dart:47) reports success. Fix: check the checkpoint result and return null (no rotation, no lastAutoBackupAt update) on busy; or copy -wal/-shm alongside; or use sqlite's VACUUM INTO, which is atomic and WAL-aware.

findings.claim: SnoozeService's read-modify-write is not transactional, so a background snooze can clobber a concurrent foreground completion's due-date advance
findings.detail: snoozeChore reads the row at :28-32 and writes at :40-41 with no enclosing transaction, unlike CompletionService.completeChore which deliberately wraps its read-modify-write (completion_service.dart:62-92) for exactly this reason. Two concurrent snoozes are benign (both compute tomorrow-at-the-same-time-of-day), but the notification isolate's snooze racing an in-app completion is not: the snooze reads nextDueDate = Jan 10, the completion transaction commits Jan 11, then the snooze writes a value derived from its stale read -- overwriting the recurrence advance and leaving the chore completed with a snooze-derived due date. Narrow window. Fix: wrap the read and write in db.transaction and re-read inside it, matching completeChore.

findings.claim: The Android widget's JSON parsing is unguarded, unlike every other platform boundary in the branch
findings.detail: onDataSetChanged (:39-43) calls parseChores(raw) with no guard, and parseChores (:76-91) uses JSONArray(raw) plus obj.getInt/getString/getBoolean, each of which throws JSONException on a malformed or shape-changed payload. onDataSetChanged runs in the app's own process (RemoteViewsService), so an uncaught throw kills it. Every Dart-side platform call in this branch is wrapped precisely to avoid this -- HomeWidgetDataWriter (widget_sync_service.dart:126-146), PluginNotificationScheduler (notification_scheduler.dart, every method), WorkManagerAutoBackupScheduler (auto_backup_scheduler.dart:20-45) -- making the Kotlin side the one unhardened boundary. Fix: wrap parseChores in try/catch and fall back to emptyList().

findings.claim: Widget rows double-prefix an emoji onto chore names that already start with one
findings.detail: chore.emoji ?? guessChoreEmoji(chore.name) is prepended unconditionally at :103-106. A chore the user named '[trash emoji] Trash' with no explicit emoji set guesses the same trash emoji from the token 'trash' (icon_guesser.dart:12) and renders in the widget as that emoji twice followed by the name. Cosmetic, and the widget row has limited width so it also eats space from an already-long name. Fix: skip the prefix when the name's first rune is already an emoji/symbol.

findings.claim: bestStreakAcrossChores presents a long-abandoned chore's historical streak as the household's current best streak
findings.detail: computeStreak (:103-120) walks newest-to-oldest and never checks that the newest completion is itself recent, and bestStreakAcrossChores does not filter either. A weekly chore completed 6 times consecutively and then abandoned 14 months ago still returns a streak of 6, which the Mission Log surfaces as the current best streak. Fix: gate on now.difference(newest) <= expectedPeriod + grace before counting a streak as current.

findings.claim: rotateAutoBackups matches on filename prefix only, ignoring the extension its own doc-comment relies on for safety
findings.detail: The comment at :9-12 justifies the .db extension as what stops rotation's directory listing sweeping up .db3 manual exports, but the predicate at :100 is basename.startsWith(kAutoBackupFilePrefix) and never inspects the extension. It is safe today only because the prefixes happen to differ (chorebuddy-auto- vs chorebuddy_backup_), so the documented invariant and the enforced one have drifted apart -- exactly the kind of prose-only guarantee that regresses silently. Related: autoBackupFileName (:36-42) has 1-second granularity, so two snapshots taken in the same second overwrite each other. Fix: add the extension to the predicate so the code enforces what the comment claims.
